title: perf: canary auto-detection for throughput/latency regressions + rollout guards
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Adds automatic detection of perf regressions for canaries and rollout guard logic; safe defaults and opt-outs.
description: Context: We run continuous performance canaries to detect regressions in throughput and P95/P99 latency before broad rollouts. Motivation: manual inspection misses transient regressions and slow regressions that only appear under specific sequence length distributions. This PR introduces automated canary regression detection and rollout guard logic that can automatically pause rollouts, trigger a rollback or route traffic to a safe model variant when statistically significant regressions are detected. What changed: 1) perf-canary service: added canary_autodetect module which consumes per-request latency, token throughput, and KV-cache hit metrics and computes rolling statistical tests (bootstrap and Thompson sampling heuristics) to detect regressions; 2) runtime scheduler: exported sequence-length segmented histograms and per-worker throughput metrics to the canary pipeline; 3) observability: new dashboards and alert rules for automated detection, including visualizations for baseline vs candidate distributions; 4) rollout controller: new guard rules and actions (pause rollout, revert to previous model, switch to lower-cost variant) with configurable thresholds and cooldown windows; 5) infra/helm: new values to opt into automated guards and define default policies. Testing: unit tests for statistical detectors, integration tests that run synthetic canary traffic with injected latency/throughput anomalies, end-to-end test that verifies rollout pause and auto-revert on a failed canary. Rollout plan: feature gated behind cluster-level flag perfCanaryAutoDetect=false by default; will be enabled for internal dogfood first, then opt-in customers, then GA after 2 weeks of stable runs. Backward compatibility: all changes are opt-in and do not affect existing canary metrics collection when disabled. Security: no sensitive data is logged. Migration: none required.
commits: feat(perf-canary): add auto-detection pipeline and statistical tests
refactor(runtime): expose sequence-length histograms to metrics endpoint
feat(rollout): implement guard rules and controller actions
test(perf-canary): add unit and integration tests
chore(helm): add opt-in flags and docs
files_changed: rollout/controller.go - new guard evaluation loop and actions
review_comments: Diego: Can you add a short doc explaining the statistical test thresholds and why we chose bootstrap+thompson? Please include references to the evaluation harness results.
Author(Avery): Added a new section in perf-canary/README.md and inline comments in autodetect.py - the thresholds are conservative by default and configurable via helm values.
Priya: We need to ensure the detection window respects KV-cache warmup behavior; otherwise short-lived spikes look like regressions.
Author: Added a warmup exclusion window and a sequence-length bucket normalization step per Priya's suggestion. Integration tests added to cover warmup scenarios.
Janelle: Confirmed CI integration test reproduces rollback action; left LGTM after a small nit on logging verbosity.
canary_rules_added: auto_detect_stat_test: bootstrap_pvalue<0.01 over 5m window triggers alert
throughput_drop_detector: >20% sustained drop over 3m with p95 increase triggers pause
safe_variant_fallback: on pause for >2m attempt variant switch once per rollout
testing_summary: Unit tests cover detector math and edge cases; integration tests simulate synthetic traffic with injected latency and throughput anomalies; e2e test validates controller pauses rollout and triggers revert/fallback under failure conditions; ran dogfood cluster for 72 hours with auto-detect enabled against non-production models and observed zero false positives after tuning.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive thresholds may cause unnecessary pauses; Mitigation: feature is opt-in, conservative defaults, cooldown windows, and manual override API. Risk: metric cardinality growth from additional histograms; Mitigation: sequence-length buckets are coarser by default and configurable. Rollback safety: controller performs a single revert action and rate-limits automatic reverts to prevent flapping.
notes: Related: ENG-4021 is the broader perf-canary initiative; ENG-4088 covers rollout controller refactors needed to support guard actions
This PR ties into the perf canary dashboards under Observability > Canaries and the SLO team reviewed thresholds.
